newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak steel maker VSZ says to diversify.
newsitem.headline: Slovak steel maker VSZ says to diversify.

text.p: Slovakia's largest steelmaker VSZ a.s. will continue its strategy of chanelling profits into diversification in order to loosen its dependence on the fickle steel market, management officials said on Monday.
"We want to focus more strongly on other sectors such as banking, automobile production and services," VSZ President Jan Smerek told a news conference in Kosice.

Smerek announced that VSZ had posted a 1.35 billion crown net profit in 1996, a nine percent increase from the 1.2 billion profit in the previous year and that management had proposed a 1996 dividend of 40 crowns per share after 30 crowns in 1995.
The 1996 profit was made on total revenues of 52.07 billion crowns.
"We saw a negative trend in revenues at the end of last year, but we were able quickly to adapt to this trend, to post satisfactory results for the full year," Smerek said.

VSZ is already diversifying into other fields in order to eliminate the negative influence of cyclical devlopments in the steel industry, and has already heavily invested in the past two years into banking, insurance, services and even sports. Last year it bought the Czech Republic's Sparta Prague football club for one billion crowns.
On Monday, the company announced it was in preliminary negotiations with an unspecified Japanese carmaker on building a car assembly plant in Slovakia.
"We are negotiating with (Japanese) Nomura Bank....but these talks are still only very preliminary," Jan Seno, VSZ Vice President for finance told Reuters.
Two years ago VSZ had begun talks on a Slovak car assembly plant with Korean KIA car producer, but these broke down, Smerek said without elaborating.
Last month VSZ Supervisory Board Chairman Alexander Rezes said VSZ was perparing extensive restructuring measures partly in the hope of forging ties with Japan's Toyota Motor Corp .
After a trip to Japan at the beginning of April, Slovak Finance Minister Sergei Kozlik said Toyota was considering locating a car production plant in eastern Slovakia.
Toyota has so far not commented on the project.
